purpose: Reveal the two final holdout velocity and dispersion fields exactly once and compare them with fixed Newtonian and simple-MOND predictions from both registered baryons and formula-independent adaptive fake twins.

observationProcessing.skyCenter: fixed SPARC/NED coordinate already used for baryonic registration
observationProcessing.systemicVelocity: one formula-independent H I-intensity-weighted central median nuisance per galaxy
observationProcessing.handedness: one formula-independent binary observation-coordinate convention per galaxy
observationProcessing.kinematicAxis: one gas-and-inverse-variance-weighted first-harmonic unit phase per galaxy, using the P0750 estimator
observationProcessing.scoreMask: finite moment 0, moment 1, and moment 2 samples with positive gas weight from one beam to H I R995
observationProcessing.uncertaintyKmS: quadrature sum of moment-2 dispersion and universal 5.2 km/s channel FWHM divided by 2.355
observationProcessing.predictionBeam: THINGS geometric-mean circular Gaussian with gas-intensity weighting

interpretation.fieldErrorRatio: gas-weighted prediction RMSE divided by gas-weighted RMS measurement-plus-dispersion uncertainty
interpretation.competitiveButIncomplete: median registered-baryon kinematic-axis ratio <= 2 and no galaxy ratio > 2
interpretation.formulaHoldoutFailure: at least one registered-baryon kinematic-axis galaxy ratio > 2
interpretation.simulatorFidelitySuccess: every adaptive-twin versus registered-baryon prediction transport RMSE <= 12 km/s

claimBoundary: P0752 is the one-shot final holdout for the current resolved-galaxy simulator and observation policy.
One kinematic phase is an observation-coordinate nuisance shared by all formulas; its fitted speed amplitude is discarded.
The formula score on registered baryons tests the gravity law; adaptive-twin transport separately tests simulator fidelity.
No inclination, distance, M/L, Newton constant, MOND scale, pressure support, warp, dark halo, or formula-specific parameter is fitted.
A holdout miss must remain visible and cannot be repaired and relabeled as holdout evidence.
